subject: SaaS subscription proration & entitlement revocation (AWS Marketplace) - next steps
content:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: procurement@datascale.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, mp-enablement@amazon.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: SaaS subscription proration & entitlement revocation (AWS Marketplace) - next steps

Hi Team (DataScale + AWS enablement),

Thanks again for the call earlier. To close the remaining items for the AWS Marketplace listing and ensure the co-sell cadence can progress, we need to confirm how entitlements and billing adjustments will be handled when customers modify seat counts mid-cycle.

High-level ask: Can we align on a proration policy and entitlement revocation behavior that works with AWS SaaS subscriptions? Specific questions below — please reply with your preferred options or redlines so we can draft the amendment.

1) Billing model: DataScale confirmed this will be a seat-based subscription sold via AWS SaaS Subscriptions (monthly renewals). We need to map Redwood's internal "seats" to the Marketplace entitlement dimension — do you prefer an additive "active_seats" gauge or an increment-only metering event?

2) Proration: If a customer removes seats mid-billing-period, do you want:
   - Option A (recommended): pro-rate credits applied immediately to the next invoice (prorated by remaining days), or
   - Option B: credits applied at the next renewal only (no intra-period credit).

3) Entitlement revocation: When an org admin removes a seat, what enforcement semantics do you expect?
   - Immediate enforcement (user token invalidated instantly), OR
   - End-of-day / scheduled enforcement (to avoid race conditions with active sessions).

4) Fulfillment payload: We'll need the following fields in the fulfillment/entitlement record so AWS can reconcile usage: account_id, entitlement_dimension (active_seats), effective_start, effective_end (nullable), quantity_delta, invoice_reference. Are there other required fields on your side?

I've attached a draft amendment that adds a simple proration clause and sample API mapping table. Also attached a CSV with a suggested proration matrix for example seat counts.

Attachments: amendment-redwood-datascale-v1.pdf (PDF, 124 KB), proration-matrix.csv (CSV, 2 KB)

Next steps: If you confirm Option A for proration and immediate revocation with a 1-hour grace window, Ben will prepare the commercial terms and Markus will push the DocuSign amendment.

Thanks,

--
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Director, Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0127

-----

From: procurement@datascale.com <procurement@datascale.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@datascale.com; mp-enablement@amazon.com
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SaaS subscription proration & entitlement revocation (AWS Marketplace) - next steps

Hi Stephanie,

Appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifying points from procurement/legal at DataScale:

- We prefer Option A (immediate proration) for seat decreases, but we need clear limits: credits should be calculated to the day and applied on the next invoice, not as immediate cash refunds.

- For entitlement revocation, our security team prefers immediate enforcement for deprovisioning; however, they asked for a short grace window (30–60 minutes) to avoid interrupting active workflows. Any longer grace period beyond 2 hours is unacceptable.

- Fulfillment payload: we need an additional field to track the customer PO (po_number) and a separate "subscription_id" that maps to our internal billing system.

We'll review the draft amendment and propose redlines by early next week.

Best,
Anika Patel
Procurement Manager
DataScale Inc
procurement@datascale.com

-----

On Fri, Jan 16, 2026 at 09:45 AM Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Anika — that all sounds reasonable.
>
> Ben / Markus: DataScale asked for credits applied on the next invoice (day-accurate proration) and immediate deprovisioning with a 30–60 minute grace window. Also add po_number and subscription_id to the fulfillment payload.
>
> Ben: please confirm commercial impact and whether we want to offer any mitigations (eg: 30-day no-proration for enterprise accounts, or a small admin fee).
>
> --Steph

-----

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, procurement@datascale.com
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SaaS subscription proration & entitlement revocation (AWS Marketplace) - next steps

Stephanie / Anika,

I discussed commercial options with Sales Ops. Recommendation: accept Option A (day-accurate proration, credits on next invoice) as the default for Marketplace orders. For enterprise accounts (annual contracts converted to Marketplace), propose an exception: no intra-period proration if customer purchases a minimum committed seat count (we'll mark this in the amendment as "non-prorated enterprise commitment").

On the enforcement side, immediate revocation with a 60-minute grace window is fine. Implementation note for infra: we should emit a "revocation_event" to the entitlement pipeline with effective_end = timestamp (UTC) and include a 60-minute "grace_ttl" attribute so frontend/SDKs can respect session windows. This plays nicely with prefix/KV cache invalidation in the runtime.

I'll model expected ARR/credit exposure for a 90-day look at the attached proration-matrix and send numbers to Anika separately.

- Ben
Director, Sales Engineering
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Attachment referenced: proration-matrix.csv (outlined examples)

-----

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@datascale.com
Date: Sun, 18 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Contract language + DocuSign flow for proration clause

Team,

I've drafted a short amendment clause to append to the existing subscription agreement for Marketplace-transacted customers. Key points:

- Define "Effective Seat Count" and an "Effective End" timestamp for seat reductions.
- Credits are calculated pro rata to the day, reflected as account credit on the customer's subsequent Marketplace invoice. No cash refunds.
- Redwood reserves the right to designate enterprise commitments as non-prorated where explicitly stated in the order form.

I added an enforceability section that covers entitlement revocation (immediate invalidation with 60-minute grace TTL) and a short data-retention paragraph (entitlement change logs retained for 24 months).

I'll upload the PDF amendment to DocuSign and share the link. For AWS fulfillment, the amendment references the entitlement_dimension "active_seats" and the required fields (account_id, subscription_id, po_number, effective_start, effective_end, quantity_delta, invoice_reference).

Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Commercial
markus_klein@redwood.ai

Attachment: amendment-redwood-datascale-v1.pdf (uploaded to DocuSign draft)

-----

From: procurement@datascale.com <procurement@datascale.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@datascale.com, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, mp-enablement@amazon.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SaaS subscription proration & entitlement revocation (AWS Marketplace) - next steps

Hi all,

Thanks — we reviewed Markus's draft and have two small redlines:

1) Please change the grace window language from a fixed 60 minutes to "up to 60 minutes" (to allow short delays for system maintenance).
2) Add explicit language that credits are "applied as account credit on the next Marketplace invoice unless otherwise agreed in writing" (just to avoid ambiguity).

We are fine with marking certain enterprise orders as non-prorated; procurement will flag those in the PO. Please send the final DocuSign packet and we'll sign.

Regards,
Anika Patel
Procurement Manager
DataScale Inc

-----

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: procurement@datascale.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: mp-enablement@amazon.com
Date: Fri, 23 Jan 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SaaS subscription proration & entitlement revocation (AWS Marketplace) - next steps

Thanks Anika — great, that's straightforward. Summary & action items: 

- Agreement: Option A proration (day-accurate), credits applied on next Marketplace invoice.
- Grace window: "up to 60 minutes" for entitlement revocation enforcement — Markus to insert that exact wording.
- Payload additions: include subscription_id and po_number in fulfillment record.
- Enterprise exception: non-prorated if called out on the PO/order form.

Action owners: 
- Markus: finalize amendment PDF + push DocuSign (target: 2026-01-26). Attachment will include the proration matrix. 
- Ben: finalize commercial note on enterprise exceptions and deliver ARR/credit exposure calc to Anika by 2026-01-25.
- Stephanie: open MPX Jira (MPX-789) to track fulfillment changes and notify AWS enablement once DocuSign is complete. HubSpot deal DS-12345 updated with amendment status.

Docs & links: DocuSign draft (https://app.docusign.com/prepare/ABC-REDWOOD-DS), HubSpot deal (https://hubspot.redwood.ai/deal/DS-12345), Jira (https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/MPX-789).

I've attached a lightweight text file with the DocuSign prep link for your legal teams: docusign-amendment-link.txt (contains the signing URL).

Thanks everyone — welcome to co-sell runway.

--
Stephanie

Attachments: docusign-amendment-link.txt
